summary.headline: Mold-Tek Q1 FY27 per-kg EBITDA rose to INR46.7 (from ~INR40.7 in FY26) on consolidation and mix, while volume grew only ~6% due to a 17% lube drop.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a record quarter, with turnover crossing INR300 crores and EBITDA per kg at INR46.7 versus INR40.7 for full FY26. The company attributes the margin gain mainly to consolidating Hyderabad units from 5 to 2, lower overheads, wastage and inter-unit transfers, and a higher share of pharma and Food & FMCG. Volume growth was about 6%, held back by a 17% fall in lube volumes linked to base-oil shortages at some clients, while paint grew 10.8% in volume and Food & FMCG and pharma grew 24% and 38%. Revenue growth was inflated by raw-material pass-through (PP copolymer rose from about INR107/kg in Q4 to about INR130/kg in Q1), and working capital and finance cost rose sharply as a result.

segments.name: Paints (decorative)
segments.commentary: Value ~46% of revenue, volume ~50% (management); volume grew 10.8% and value ~31%, with growth from existing clients and rising IML adoption. Management expects paint's share to fall toward ~40% over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Lubes
segments.commentary: Volume fell 17% due to base-oil shortages at some private clients affected by the Iran war; lube EBITDA is about INR35-40/kg. Management expects recovery in the current quarter.

segments.name: Food & FMCG (incl. Qpack)
segments.commentary: Food & FMCG grew 24.2% (26% per analyst); Food is ~24% of sales and ~28-29% including Qpack. Management targets 18-20% CAGR.

segments.name: Qpack
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to ~2% from ~20% in the prior quarter because edible oil and cashew customers were price-sensitive; some customers moved back to tin. Management expects ~10% growth in Q2 and double digits later.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Revenue up 41% (volume up 38%) YoY; FY26 base INR34 crores with FY27 target INR50-55 crores. Pharma is ~3.5% of sales but only ~2% of volume.

segments.name: Vibe (JV)
segments.commentary: Three products have patent applications and further products are at pilot stage; commercial products expected around Q3 FY27, with a couple of crores of revenue possible in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA per kg target raised to INR44-45 (from INR42-43); management says it expects to beat INR42 comfortably.
Volume growth target of 10-12% for FY27; management says ~10% is achievable and paint could grow 10-15%.
FY27 capex cut to ~INR90 crores (from INR130-135 crores), including INR25-30 crores for pharma.
Management expects EBITDA growth of 18-20% with volume growth near 10%, and sees the 19-20% EBITDA growth as sustainable for the rest of the year.
Capacity additions of 10-12% a year; target to lift utilisation from ~75% to 78-80%, plus 8-10% new capacity.
capex_capacity: Total capacity is ~67,000 MTPA across Cheyyar, Panipat and Mahad; management says utilisation is about 75%.
Panipat thin-wall trials on 4 machines sell INR70 lakhs-1 crore a month, doubling from August; Qpack sales from Panipat were INR1-1.5 crores in the last six months.
Ophthalmic range: 25,000 sq ft building under construction at the current facility, due in ~6 months; commercial molds are 5-6 months away. Trial molds are complete.

Medical devices (dosing pens): planned minimum capacity of 1 million pens per month; the new land is reserved for devices, and a plant needs 50,000-60,000 sq ft, INR10 crores building and INR10-15 crores machinery.
Automation and lean-manufacturing study planned with a Chinese partner, with implementation expected in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Raw-material costs were passed through to clients in the following month; management says the company recovered the full increase while keeping margins.
PP copolymer price peaked near INR155-160/kg in late March/April, was ~INR145-146/kg at the time of the call, and management expects it could fall to INR120-125/kg if the war ends.
Inventory gain in Q1 estimated at INR1-1.5/kg.
Realisation benefit: management said ~INR3/kg came from higher pharma and FMCG realisation and ~INR3/kg from consolidation and efficiencies.
Raw-material availability is better than in March-April, though pricing remains volatile. Company inventory is about 1 month (raw material, SFG and finished goods).

qa_highlights.question: What is the ideal long-term revenue mix, and what share will decorative paints fall to?
qa_highlights.answer: Paint is ~46% of value and ~50% of volume today; management expects it to settle around 40% over 3-4 years as Food & FMCG, Qpack and pharma outgrow paint (paint growing 8-10% vs pharma 40-50% CAGR).

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only ~6%, and how sustainable is the INR46.7/kg EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Lube volume fell 17% on base-oil shortages at some private clients (Iran war), costing ~3 points of volume growth; ex-lube volume would have been ~9%. EBITDA/kg gain attributed to Hyderabad consolidation (5 to 2 units), lower overheads, wastage and inter-unit transfers; FY27 EBITDA/kg target raised to INR44-45.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Qpack growth slow to ~2%, and why did pharma volume only rise ~2-3% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Qpack customers in edible oil and cashew were price-sensitive after raw material rose from ~INR100 to ~INR150/kg; some moved back to tin. Management expects ~10% Qpack growth in Q2 and double digits later. Pharma grew 41% in revenue (38% volume), with a quarterly run-rate of INR11-12 crores and a FY27 target of INR50-55 crores against INR34 crores in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise ~20% QoQ if no new term debt was planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher working capital from raw-material prices, not term loans. Raw material moved from ~INR97/kg (FY26 average) and ~INR107 in Q4 to ~INR130 in Q1; working capital rose to ~INR125 crores from ~INR110-112 crores at end-March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Vibe JV and when will commercial volumes start?
qa_highlights.answer: Three products have patent applications filed and more are in pilot, expected in about 2 months. Commercial products are expected around Q3 FY27, with a couple of crores of revenue possible in FY27 and decent numbers next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down (46.6% to 41.3%) despite a ~46% revenue jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue inflation reflects raw-material pass-through; EBITDA/kg rose ~INR6 YoY (INR40.7 to INR46.7), which it cited as proof of efficiency gains. Inventory gain in Q1 estimated at INR1-1.5/kg.

qa_highlights.question: How much of sales-per-kg growth is price versus mix, and what did consolidation and mix each add to EBITDA/kg?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was up 6.25%, so most of the ~19% sales-per-kg growth is inflation (at least ~15%); mix adds the rest. Realisation from pharma and FMCG added ~INR3/kg and consolidation and efficiencies ~INR3/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What are the plans for new capacity, the ophthalmic and device businesses, and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is ~67,000 MTPA at ~75% utilisation; management plans 10-12% capacity addition a year and to lift utilisation to 78-80%. A 25,000 sq ft ophthalmic building is due in ~6 months. Devices (minimum 1 million pens/month) need 50,000-60,000 sq ft, INR10 crores building and INR10-15 crores machinery. FY27 capex cut to ~INR90 crores from INR130-135 crores; Q1 capex was INR20-22 crores.

risks_watch: Raw-material volatility: PP copolymer at ~INR145-146/kg versus a ~INR155-160 peak; management expects ~INR120-125 if the war ends, and pass-through lags by a month, so margin % and gross margin are noisy.
Lube recovery: volume fell 17% on base-oil shortages; management expects recovery this quarter, but the outcome depends on clients' alternative base-oil supply.
Qpack price sensitivity: growth slowed to ~2% and some customers moved back to tin; management expects ~10% growth in Q2.
Finance cost and working capital: finance cost up ~20% QoQ and working capital at ~INR125 crores; the trend depends on raw-material prices.
Execution on new lines: ophthalmic building due in ~6 months, device partner/IP route unresolved (1 year vs 2-3 years), Vibe commercial launch targeted for Q3 FY27.

Sustainability of EBITDA/kg: management holds INR44-45 for FY27 but flagged possible marginal dips if utilisation or Qpack do not recover; the INR46.7 Q1 figure includes inventory gains of INR1-1.5/kg.
key_quotes: So this consolidation and improved sales of high-margin products has enhanced our EBITDA margins considerably in spite of the economic disturbance all around the globe due to the war situation.
Consolidation of units is a onetime thing, but its benefits will last forever.
So lube is a disappointing performance this quarter, which is beyond our hands because of the input problems of oil -- base oil to the -- some of the private players.
It's not because of term loans.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on EBITDA per kg and consolidation, and raised FY27 guidance. It was more cautious and deflecting on volume, lubes, Qpack and raw-material price direction, repeatedly pointing to war-related factors beyond its control.
